op.description: probe = only detect engines/packages/licences (never runs user code); run = execute; receipt = re-render/complete an existing receipt idempotently; install = two-step plan/confirm package installation

mode.description: op=run feeding mode; 'expr' is refused for engine=cli

code.description: mode=code: source text; the tool writes it to Computation/<runId>/script.<ext> before executing

file.description: mode=file: project-relative script path (path-guarded); op=receipt: a receipt id or script path

expr.description: mode=expr: a single expression, substituted into ONE argv element by the assembler (never shell-concatenated)

packages.description: packages/toolboxes that must exist; ['refresh'] forces a re-probe in op=probe

timeoutMs.description: per-run budget; defaults to params.mathTimeoutMs (60000), clamped to >= 1000

captureFiles.description: project-relative files copied into the receipt after the run (read-only copy; must stay inside the project)

record.description: default true: write Computation/<runId>/ (script, outputs, receipt.json/.md)

cli.description: required when engine='cli': { command, argv[], stdin? }

scope.description: op=install only. Defaults to params.mathInstallScope ('user'). 'system' must be given on EVERY call and is never remembered.

dryRun.description: op=install: default true -> return the plan + planToken without executing

confirm.description: op=install: the planToken returned by the dry run, echoed verbatim; executing with a mismatched/expired token is REFUSED

runtimeValidation.reason: v2/v3/v4 register tools bare (additionalProperties:false is NOT enforced at runtime on v4 - v4:3034), so the module validates args itself and returns MATH_INVALID_ARGUMENT (never throws)

probe.returns: engines[] (available, path, version, licence), packages{}, cached:boolean
probe.notes: cache is per process; 'refresh' in packages forces a re-probe; missing engines come back with the user-install guide (§3.1 of the spec)

modes.code: write code to Computation/<runId>/script.<ext>, then execute
modes.file: path-guard the project-relative file, copy it into Computation/<runId>/script.<ext>, then execute
modes.expr: substitute expr into the engine eval template as ONE argv element; refused for engine=cli

run.guard: script path must normalise inside <projectRoot> (same containment rule as leanAbsPath, vibe-math-v2.js:635-644)

receipt.behaviour: re-render receipt.md and fill missing artefacts for an existing Computation/<runId>/ (idempotent, same semantics as the paper receipt: vibe-math-v2.js:2707-2725)

install.systemScope: explicit per call, never remembered, never defaulted
install.commercialEngines: REFUSED{reason:'commercial'} - vendor guidance only, never installed
install.planToken: sha256(engine|packages|scope|commands|planVersion) - content-derived, no wall clock; TTL = params.mathPlanTtlMs (900000)
install.audit: Computation/installs/<planToken>.json + .md: plan, scope, manager, commands, exit, before/after versions, installed[], uninstall commands, network:'not-enforced-by-plugin'
install.rollback: no general rollback; the audit records the exact commands + before/after versions so an uninstall is verifiable

returnShell.message: human-readable one-liner (safe to show the model)

failureCodes.next: per-OS user-install guide + agent install plan hint

failureCodes.when: engine found but its licence probe fails (commercial engines)
failureCodes.next: vendor link + activation instructions; NEVER an install plan

failureCodes.when: engine found but the version probe fails and it is not commercial

failureCodes.next: agent install plan (dry run) with the missing names
narrow the computation; the partial output is recorded
stderr tail is returned; no automatic retry

failureCodes.when: path escape, policy conflict (cli/shell with mathMode='typed', engine not in mathEngines), cli without command, expr on cli, or install without a matching confirm token | op:'receipt' with no archive on disk (next.reason='archive-missing')

the engine exited with a usage/option error (stderr matches unknown option|invalid option|unrecognized|usage:, or non-zero exit with usage-like output) - typical for a version-mismatched commercial template
failureCodes.next: { kind: 'engine-override', engine, argv: [<the exact argv used>], hint: 'mathEngineOverride' } - never a bare NONZERO_EXIT

failureCodes.when: schema/enum/range validation failed | op:'receipt' with an unparsable receipt.json (next.reason='receipt-unparsable')
the host exposes no subprocess service
failureCodes.next: note: record the conclusion without execution

warnings.meaning: ok:true plus truncated flags; re-run with a narrower output rather than treating it as a failure
mode:'file': the source file's current hash differs from the previous receipt's scriptHash - the old receipt does NOT represent the current code; the run was written as a new attempt
mode:'file': the source file changed between the pre-run and post-run hash (another member edited it); re-run before citing this receipt
Computation/ has passed the documented cap (20 attempts per archive id, 200 run dirs per project); the tool only warns and NEVER deletes

archiveSemantics.discoverability: every run returns and records scriptPath + scriptHash; mode:'code' writes the script to Computation/<runId>/script.<ext> and the agent may open/edit it with normal file tools
archiveSemantics.rerunRule: after editing, re-run with mode:'file' to produce a NEW receipt; an old receipt must not be cited as evidence for edited code (the prompt text says this explicitly)
archiveSemantics.runId: runId = <preset>-<projectSlug>-<sha256(engine|mode|KEY|sorted(packages))[0:12]>; KEY is the SOURCE PATH for mode:'file' (file:<rel>) and the canonical script text otherwise; no wall clock
archiveSemantics.appendOnly: attempt 1 lives in Computation/<id>/ and is never rewritten; attempt n>=2 lives in Computation/<id>/attempts/<n>/ (first free n); existing files are never overwritten
archiveSemantics.reconciliation: mode:'file' runs and op:'receipt' compare the recorded scriptHash with the current hash and report scriptChanged; a file run additionally hashes before and after the run and reports scriptChangedDuringRun
archiveSemantics.receiptOp: op:'receipt' is read-only: it re-checks the hash, returns the recorded + current hashes, and only writes a MISSING receipt.md - it never rewrites existing receipt files
archiveSemantics.retention: cap = MATH_ARCHIVE_MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_RUN (20) and MATH_ARCHIVE_MAX_RUNS (200, checked only when the host exposes the optional listDir); over the cap = warn only, never auto-delete
archiveSemantics.concurrency: same-archive-id allocation + the claiming receipt.json write are serialised by an in-process per-id promise chain, so two concurrent runs of one id take attempt 1 and attempt 2 and never share a directory; cross-process concurrency still needs an exclusive-create primitive from the host (docs §6)
archiveSemantics.failClosed: a source file that disappears mid-run sets scriptChangedDuringRun:true (null !== before hash); op:receipt reports scriptChanged:true when the archived script cannot be read
archiveSemantics.pathGuard: projectRel is LEXICAL only (rejects absolute/drive/.. escapes) and does not resolve symlinks/junctions; real containment belongs to the host fs (resolve/contains)
archiveSemantics.verificationBoundary: engine execution, real argv/version/licence paths and installers are verified ONLY through the fake subprocess seam, never against real engines
archiveSemantics.receiptOpMissingArchive: op:receipt for a missing archive directory/receipt.json returns MATH_REFUSED with next:{kind:reason, reason:archive-missing}; an unparsable receipt.json stays MATH_INVALID_ARGUMENT (receipt-unparsable)
archiveSemantics.hashLimits: scriptChanged/scriptChangedDuringRun are CONTENT hashes by design: a same-content replacement (different inode/mtime) and a truncate-then-restore are indistinguishable and cannot be reported
archiveSemantics.instanceLifetime: per-session module instances live exactly as long as their session object (pre-existing preset lifecycle, not introduced by P2a or the audit fixes)

paramNamesFrozen.costOfRenamingLater: 4 presets x 5-6 wiring sites + v5 closed-set vibe_v5_set + visibleParams + both persona blocks + prompt-corpus-persona/* + prompt-corpus-vN/* + bilingual README tables + docs/math-computation.md

mathMode.meaning: prompt policy ONLY (the plugin cannot enforce it: subprocess.spawn has no policy slot). With 'typed+shell' the prompt may suggest the host shell as a fallback, but shell runs carry no receipt and no limit guarantees and MUST be marked 'not tool-archived'; 'typed' never mentions the shell and also refuses engine='cli'

mathEngines.meaning: SageMath is P2. 'cli' is ON BY DEFAULT (ruling 2): it is no broader than the host shell the model already has and still goes through limits/cwd/receipts. Disable it by removing 'cli' here or by setting mathMode='typed' (then engine='cli' returns REFUSED{reason:'policy'})

mathInstallScope.meaning: 'system' is per call only and is never persisted

mathEngineOverride.meaning: per-engine overrides of versionArgv/scriptArgv/evalArgv/packageProbe - the supported escape hatch for commercial CLI drift (Maple templates ship flagged VERIFY)

policyInteractions.shellFallback: not enforceable by the plugin (subprocess.spawn has no policy slot, vibe-math-v5.js:2096-2100); mathMode only decides what the prompt advertises. Real enforcement needs host sandbox/policy support - recorded as a pending upstream requirement (spec R9), out of scope for this round
policyInteractions.cliEscapeHatch: engine='cli' is a TOOL path: it goes through the same cwd/timeout/output-cap/receipt pipeline and is recorded as 'cli:<command>'. It is ON BY DEFAULT because the model already has a host shell under mathMode='typed+shell'; cli is therefore no broader, but it does leave a receipt and respects limits. Disable via mathMode='typed' or by omitting 'cli' from mathEngines; it is NOT the raw host shell
policyInteractions.evidence: only tool-routed runs produce Computation/<runId>/ receipts; raw shell runs produce nothing and must be labelled un-archived
policyInteractions.argvEcho: every run writes the exact argv into receipt.argv and echoes it in the return shell, so a version-mismatched template is diagnosable; a usage/option error returns MATH_ENGINE_BAD_ARGV with next.kind='engine-override'

refusalVocabulary.note: EXHAUSTIVE (guarded by tests/audit-math-computation-parity.mjs): every literal the module can emit, and every literal must be written as a STRING LITERAL so the vocabulary stays machine-extractable. Renaming/adding one without updating here turns the parity guard red.
